name: Cellular Base-Station Aggregation Nodes
description: Many cellular/base-station registries -> one deconflicted SDS $TBS site stream. Three pure flow nodes: `route` turns one $HTQ request into N hostcap/http-request GET descriptors for the provider set the CALLER named plus the run contract; `parse` decodes each provider native payload into normalized reports; `deconflict` merges reports across providers under the caller chosen tbsMergeMethod and emits a size-prefixed $TBS record stream plus a run summary. Configuration is REQUEST-SCOPED, never node-global, so two callers can ask for different provider sets at once without either changing what the node is. NO CAPABILITIES, deliberately: this plugin performs no I/O — http is the generic hostcap connector node, and the credential lane (keyslot.unwrap + secrets.put/clear) is a SEPARATE wasmedge-only plugin, cell-tower-credentials, so the grants an operator makes for credentials never attach to the code that parses provider bodies and stays browser-testable.

sequentialJustification.detail: All three methods are single-pass transforms over frames the flow hands them: `route` formats fetch descriptors from the request, `parse` walks each provider body once, and `deconflict` groups reports and emits one record per group. There is no shared mutable state, no worker pool and no fan-out inside the guest — the fan-out is the flow's, across N http connector nodes. This guest can never spawn a thread, so it compiles clang/wasi-sequential rather than claiming a wasi-threads contract it does not honour.

methods.description: Decodes the one $HTQ envelope the host delivers and dispatches on METHOD+PATH, because the host mounts ONE http trigger per flow and all HTTP semantics live in-wasm. /providers builds the provider catalog and hands it to the credential mediator to finish (key slot + per-lane configured flags); /credentials/<providerId> validates the provider against the compiled registry, derives the lane id and forwards the sealed envelope to the mediator, refusing an unknown provider or a wrong verb here without any capability; every other path is the aggregation, reading PROVIDERS/METHOD/LIMIT from the body and emitting one hostcap/http-request descriptor per selected provider plus the run contract. An unknown METHOD is REFUSED on the reply port rather than silently defaulted; providers requiring a login are skipped with an explicit reason.

wildcardJustification.detail: Provider catalog handed to the flow's http-respond node. Source METADATA (ids, access posture, licence, whether a lane is configured), not observation data, so no SDS record type describes it and inventing one would be worse than naming it what it is.

outputPorts.description: Provider catalog, emitted when the request PATH is the catalog route.

acceptedTypeSets.description: UTF-8 JSON task for the credential mediator.

wildcardJustification.detail: One of {op:catalog, catalog:<the catalog this node built>}, {op:put, providerId, lane, envelope:<the browser keyslot envelope, verbatim and unread>} or {op:clear, providerId, lane}. Control routing between two nodes of one flow, not observation data; no SDS record describes a request-scoped instruction and inventing one would be worse than naming it what it is.

outputPorts.description: Task for the credential mediator, emitted when the request PATH is the catalog route or the credential route.

methods.description: Decodes each provider's native payload into normalized reports, dropping rows whose coordinates are out of range rather than clamping them. A provider whose fetch failed contributes nothing but stays in providers_consulted, so 'asked and got nothing' never reads as 'agreed'.

inputPorts.description: The run contract. Delivered EXACTLY ONCE per run, on the first invocation, and never re-delivered (the runtime FIFO-consumes it). It must therefore be OPTIONAL: while it was required:true, draining that single frame left this node permanently unready and every later response queued forever, unconsumed and unreported. Cached in module state on arrival.

acceptedTypeSets.description: hostcap/http-request response, one frame per provider: normally an aligned binary $HRB raw-body-v1 frame (status plus verbatim body), with legacy JSON/bodyB64 accepted for compatibility.

wildcardJustification.detail: hostcap/http-request response frame ($HRB raw-body-v1, or legacy {status,headers,bodyB64}) consumed inside this flow; the shape is defined by that generic connector, not by SDS.

inputPorts.description: HTTP responses, one per request descriptor route emitted. NOT capped at 1: the fan-out is one descriptor per provider URL including mirrors, and a cap of 1 delivered only the first, which is why a two-provider request returned exactly the first-named provider's answer. raw-body-v1 is used to avoid the 4/3 base64 expansion and duplicate JSON/string buffers that previously exhausted a 128 MiB WasmEdge instance on the 27 MiB BAKOM document.

acceptedTypeSets.description: UTF-8 JSON array of normalized per-provider reports.

wildcardJustification.detail: Normalized intermediate produced and consumed inside this flow. It is deliberately NOT $TBS: a single provider's unreconciled report cannot satisfy the standard's required CONSENSUS, and emitting one would assert a deconfliction that has not happened.

methods.description: Groups reports across providers by network identity (falling back to proximity where a provider publishes no identifiers) and merges each group under the caller's tbsMergeMethod, emitting one $TBS record per site with every contributing provider in SOURCES and the merge recorded in CONSENSUS. Semantics mirror packages/cell-towers-worldwide/src/deconflict.mjs and are parity-gated against it.
